short: The Wessex king who held off the Danes and laid the groundwork for one kingdom.
full:
Alfred inherited Wessex in April 871, in the middle of a Danish invasion that had already destroyed the kingdoms of Northumbria, East Anglia and Mercia. In 878 he was driven into the Somerset marshes at Athelney, regrouped, and defeated Guthrum's army at Edington. The treaty that followed partitioned England, leaving the Danelaw to the north and east and Wessex intact.

The rest of the reign was spent making that survival permanent. Alfred built a network of fortified burhs no more than a day's march apart, reorganised the fyrd so that half the levy was always under arms, and ordered a fleet built to meet raiders at sea. He imported scholars, translated Latin works into English himself, and issued a law code drawing on earlier Anglo-Saxon custom. By his death in October 899 he was styled king of the Anglo-Saxons, and his descendants would go on to rule a single English kingdom.
